html:
A court chronicle in Malay that tells the story of the Malacca Sultanate from its legendary origins to its fall to the Portuguese in 1511. It is one of the classics of Malay literature.

Its original title means "Genealogy of Kings". The oldest known version dates its writing to 1612, at the court of Johor, the kingdom founded by Malacca's exiled royal family. It is traditionally credited to the court official Tun Sri Lanang. It traces the kings back to Alexander the Great, known as Iskandar Zulkarnain, tells how Sang Nila Utama founded Singapura, and follows the founding of Malacca by Parameswara.

It is less a record of dates than a guide to how a Malay court worked: the bond between ruler and subjects, the rule that a ruler must not shame them and they must never rebel. It mixes legend with real people and events, and it ends with the Portuguese conquest. A copy collected by Stamford Raffles is among the most studied.
sum: A court chronicle in Malay that tells the story of the Malacca Sultanate from its legendary origins to its fall to the Portuguese in 1511. It is one of the classics of Malay literature.
